results.title: QXO Announces Agreement to Acquire Beacon for $11B | Industrial Distribution
results.description: After nearly a century in business — and months of often-contentious negotiations — building materials distributor Beacon will be acquired by newly formed company QXO in a deal worth about $11 billion, company officials announced Thursday.
extra_snippets: After nearly a century in business — and months of often-contentious negotiations — building materials distributor Beacon will be acquired by newly formed company QXO in a deal worth about $11 billion, company officials announced Thursday.

Under the agreement announced Thursday, QXO would acquire Beacon and its outstanding debt for $124.35 per share in cash. The transaction is expected to close by the end of April, subject to a majority of Beacon shares tendering in the current offer and other closing conditions.

Beacon officials had maintained for months that QXO’s $11 billion offers “significantly” undervalued the company and its future prospects, but Beacon Chairman Stuart Randle said in a statement that after evaluating “strategic alternatives” since the initial offer in November, a “comprehensive review” led to the conclusion that the deal “is in the best interests of Beacon and its shareholders given the immediate premium and certainty of value in cash it offers, particularly in an uncertain environment.”
QXO, established last year by former XPO head Brad Jacobs and other backers, originally sought to buy Beacon in November after an initial bid for Rexel was rejected.
